headline: Tk 3 lakh debt: Businessman found buried beneath house in Lalbagh
summary: Police recovered the body of Sheikh Wasim Roni from a balcony area of a five-story building after a friend was detained for suspected murder.
details: Police recovered the body of businessman Sheikh Wasim Roni from beneath the ground on a balcony of a five-story building in the BC Das Street area of Lalbagh, Dhaka.
The operation began around 11:30 PM on Thursday and continued until 5:30 AM on Friday morning, when the body was finally unearthed.
According to police and the victim's family, the suspect, Masum Chowdhury, had borrowed Tk 3 lakh from Roni.
It is suspected that Masum killed Roni and buried him beneath the house after Roni pressured him to return the borrowed money.
Lalbagh Police have detained Masum Chowdhury in connection with the case. The body has been sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
caption:
A businessman was found buried under a house in Lalbagh after he allegedly pressured a friend to return a borrowed Tk 3 lakh.

Police recovered the body of businessman Sheikh Wasim Roni from beneath the ground on a balcony of a five-story building in the BC Das Street area of Lalbagh, Dhaka.

The operation began around 11:30 PM on Thursday and continued until 5:30 AM on Friday morning, when the body was finally unearthed.

According to police and the victim's family, the suspect, Masum Chowdhury, had borrowed Tk 3 lakh from Roni.

It is suspected that Masum killed Roni and buried him beneath the house after Roni pressured him to return the borrowed money.

Lalbagh Police have detained Masum Chowdhury in connection with the case. The body has been sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline_marked: Green chilies hit 160 BDT/kg as [[essential food prices spike]] in Dhaka
headline: Green chilies hit 160 BDT/kg as essential food prices spike in Dhaka
summary: Vegetables, fish, and eggs are seeing abnormal price hikes, leaving low-income families struggling to afford basic protein and nutrients.
details: Prices of essential commodities in Dhaka's markets are rising sharply. Green chilies, which were 120 BDT per kg last week, have jumped to 160 BDT per kg, while eggplants are now selling for 160 to 170 BDT per kg.
Other vegetables like cucumbers, tomatoes, and bitter gourds are also more expensive. Pointed gourd, ridge gourd, and sponge gourd are now priced between 60 and 70 BDT per kg.
The fish market remains expensive, with freshwater fish costing between 800 and 1,000 BDT per kg. Cultured fish like Rui and Katla are not available for less than 400-450 BDT per kg.
Hilsa fish is available but demand is low due to high prices; 700-800 gram fish are selling for 2,000 BDT per kg, while larger ones exceed 3,000 BDT per kg.
Eggs have remained abnormally high for over a month, costing around 150 BDT per dozen. Traders claim production has dropped due to heatwaves and load shedding, though consumers disagree.
Sellers attribute the price hikes to reduced supply, while consumers complain that a lack of monitoring prevents sellers from hiking prices at will.
caption:
Green chilies jumped from 120 to 160 BDT per kg in just one week. Basic food prices are spiraling.

Prices of essential commodities in Dhaka's markets are rising sharply. Green chilies, which were 120 BDT per kg last week, have jumped to 160 BDT per kg, while eggplants are now selling for 160 to 170 BDT per kg.

Other vegetables like cucumbers, tomatoes, and bitter gourds are also more expensive. Pointed gourd, ridge gourd, and sponge gourd are now priced between 60 and 70 BDT per kg.

The fish market remains expensive, with freshwater fish costing between 800 and 1,000 BDT per kg. Cultured fish like Rui and Katla are not available for less than 400-450 BDT per kg.

Hilsa fish is available but demand is low due to high prices; 700-800 gram fish are selling for 2,000 BDT per kg, while larger ones exceed 3,000 BDT per kg.

Eggs have remained abnormally high for over a month, costing around 150 BDT per dozen. Traders claim production has dropped due to heatwaves and load shedding, though consumers disagree.

Sellers attribute the price hikes to reduced supply, while consumers complain that a lack of monitoring prevents sellers from hiking prices at will.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
